why: Turnout mobilisation, good-news and bad-news (corruption, audit) information, and persuasion messages all sit here, so signs track content and outcome, not a dispute; C00402 and W2009710863 are two versions of one Mexico experiment.

Twelve different historical exposures (mita, slave trade, concessions, treaty ports, sugar factories, ancestry) share one outcome label; the one like-for-like tension is forced-labour extraction, C00001 (mita, negative) against C02487 (Cultivation System, positive).

Outcome-side polarity: every enforcement card raises compliance, but C01372 and W1506056549 are signed on under-reporting or evasion (down) while the rest use compliance or revenue (up); C00165 and C00623 study the tax rate, not enforcement.

Event studies mostly find ties raise firm value; C00019 is negative only because its event was bad news for Suharto (implying positive value), leaving the Cheney null (C00197) and the Malaysian crisis loss (W3122513589) as genuine but event-specific dissent.

Populism cards agree that status threat and cultural backlash raise populist voting, but C00312 signs moral universalism and C00878 signs high status, the opposite ends of the cause; C02122 (outgroup removal) and C00231 (social image) ask other questions.

Same relationship, no framing problem: five studies find benefits raise incumbent support, Uganda grants (C01138) and NREGS exposure (C01241) find the reverse, and C00460 finds Progresa's earlier positive result was a data-merge error, contradicting C00226.

A grab-bag of 'other' causes (SOE reform, crop-pest mismatch, sparrows, instability); the one like-for-like pair, W2019856397 (equality raises growth) and C00982 (inequality lowers it), agrees once framed on one end; C02727 is inventor patenting.

Signs follow the medium and the outcome: newspapers raise turnout while TV and broadband crowd out news and lower it, and the other three cards measure Forza Italia votes, ticket-splitting and incumbent votes after audits.

All five show slanted media moving votes toward the side it favours, but C02311 signs the outcome as FDR's vote share, the target of Coughlin's attack, so it is negative; on the slant-favoured side it agrees.

The genuine conflict is C00899 (a local football win lifts the incumbent 1.6pp) against C00897 (shark attacks do nothing), both tests of irrelevant events; C02638 is a lab pivotal-voter game and C00841 a relevant bad-news shock.

Same relationship (roads, electrification, services and incumbent vote), no framing issue: four studies find a reward, C01172 finds better services cut ANC support, and C00663 finds PMGSY roads had no effect, contradicting C00656 on the same programme.

Each card tests a different rule on a different outcome (touch-screens and Republican share, compulsory and early voting on turnout, vote-by-mail on party share, number of offices on turnout), so mixed signs are not one dispute.

Outcome-side polarity: C00241 is signed on teacher absence (down 21pp) though test scores rose 0.17sd like the three performance-pay RCTs; the Indonesian null (C00661) is unconditional pay, a different treatment.

Unrelated causes of roll-call behaviour (media-attention shocks, factor mobility, alphabetical order, party pressure); only C02620 against W3124631225 (does party pressure matter) test one relationship, a genuine two-paper dispute.

Mixes rainfall-driven income falls (C00411), trade integration with democracies (C02336) and the long-run income-level modernisation tests (C00774, W3123123937, both null), so no two cards test one relationship.

Same relationship (democracy and growth) with democracy the cause in every card: within-country transition studies find faster growth while Barro finds a weakly negative effect and Przeworski et al. none, the classic cross-section versus panel split.

Three studies, not four (C00156 and C02449 are the RES and NBER versions of Dal Bo-Rossi): term length in Argentina, tier in Italy and final-term limits in US states invoke opposite mechanisms but vary different things.

Same relationship (local migrant or refugee presence and far-right vote), same framing of the cause: three studies of large or sudden inflows find gains while C02108 finds a small reception centre cut Front National growth, a genuine conflict that fits contact theory.

Each card studies a different shock and a different vote (mortgage defaults and the 2008 housing bill, Chinese imports and trade bills, disasters and donor-aligned votes, trade openness and immigration votes).

C01199 is signed on school attendance (which rose) although its infant-death estimate is negative like C00336, so on infant mortality the two agree once flipped; the genuine dispute left is C01908, which finds democracy has little or no effect on infant and child mortality.

Retrospective voting framed from opposite ends: C00573 and C00853 sign a positive income shock or growth (incumbent gains) while C00948 signs trade-related job losses (incumbent loses); put on the same end, all three say good economic news helps the incumbent.

Three unrelated causes of subjective well-being (prosocial spending, social relationships and personality, degree of monetisation); the sign differences come from the different causes, not from disagreement on one relationship.

Epidemiological-approach papers on different causes: ancestral-country female labour-force participation and fertility predict US women's work and fertility (C00137, W1559355478, both positive), while historic plough use lowers fertility (C01030); the sign gap is the cause studied, not disagreement.

Treatment framed from opposite ends: C01012 and C01424 sign an adverse weather shock (conflict up) while C00074 signs rainfall-instrumented growth (conflict down); all three say a negative income shock raises conflict, so C00074 should be flipped to the adverse-shock framing.

Three unrelated relationships (lifetime growth experience and trust in government, house-price gains and support for redistribution, supply-chain integration and firms' trade-agreement positions); C02024 measures firm lobbying positions, not citizens' beliefs.

C01015 randomises a direct incentive to attend (later attendance rises through friends' participation) while C00258 and C02271 randomise beliefs about total turnout (own participation falls); different treatments, and C00258 and C02271 are the QJE and NBER versions of the same Cantoni et al. experiment, so the cell holds two studies, not three.
